body.statement:
For every fixed \(c>0\), every \(P\) satisfying \(\mathrm{ass{:}positive\text{-}observed\text{-}cells}\), and every \(\Delta\), the independently model-defined legal fibers obey
\[
 (\log c,\Delta)\in\Theta_{\mathrm w}(P)
 \Longleftrightarrow\mathcal F_c^{\mathrm w}(P,\Delta)\ne\varnothing,
 \qquad
 (\log c,\Delta)\in\Theta_+(P)
 \Longleftrightarrow\mathcal F_c^+(P,\Delta)\ne\varnothing.
\]
The weak certificate uses exactly fifty-six scalar lift variables, eight \(3\times3\) PSD blocks, and eight augmented \(4\times4\) PSD blocks; the strict certificate uses sixty-four variables and eight additional \(6\times6\) common-Hankel-range blocks.  In the forward direction, each legal \((\mu,h,g)\in\mathcal M_v(c)\) is mapped to the eight joint response measures \(d\nu_{(x,r_0,r_1)}=h_xg_{x0}(r_0,\cdot)g_{x1}(r_1,\cdot)d\mu\), and then to \(d\rho_s=D_c^{-1}d\nu_s\) and its five quartic moments.  In the reverse direction, every feasible lift yields positive-half-line representing measures \((\rho_s)_{s\in S}\); after setting \(d\nu_s=D_c d\rho_s\), the construction \(\mu=\sum_{s\in S}\nu_s\) and the Radon--Nikodym reconstructions produce one unconditional probability law together with legal sequential initial and feedback kernels that generate exactly \(P\) and \(\Delta\).  For \(v=+\), the common-Hankel-range blocks yield representing measures on one positive-node set with strictly positive type weights, so the reconstructed \(h_x\) and \(g_{xy}\) satisfy the strict legal class.  When \(q_x>0\), the weak equivalence is an exact finite-dimensional representation of the \(T=2\) Bonhomme--Dano--Graham unrestricted-feedback, unrestricted-measure fiber after adjoining the observed margins \(q_x\) and applying the conditional-law translation in \(\mathrm{lem{:}bdg\text{-}weak\text{-}fiber\text{-}translation}\).  The strict fiber is an additional subclass, not a second copy of that weak published fiber.  Here unrestricted heterogeneity means an arbitrary probability law on the continuous state space \((0,\infty)\); exact correspondence with a separately imposed Lebesgue-density specialization would require an additional absolutely-continuous representation theorem and is not established by the atomic converse.
body.justification: The two-sided finite certificate equals the independently model-defined causal fiber; its all-laws strengthening proves that zero observed cells and zero-mass weak types remain legal.
body.gap: The closest published weak program remains infinite-dimensional. The exact comparison requires adjoining \(q_x\) and translating conditional laws; the strict class is additional and a Lebesgue-density replacement theorem is not proved.
body.consumer: The cone supplies grid-free, sharp slope--APE feasibility for the two-wave predetermined-children labor-participation design.
body.proof_tex:
Let \(c>0\), let \(P\) satisfy the displayed positive-cell condition, and fix \(\Delta\in\mathbb R\).  In particular \(P\in\Delta^{15}\).  The two model-to-lift and lift-to-model equivalences, all stated forward and reverse constructions, strict common-support reconstruction, singular weak cases, and variable and block counts follow from \(\mathrm{thm{:}exact\text{-}feedback\text{-}cone\text{-}all\text{-}laws}\), which proves them for every probability vector and therefore does not consume cellwise positivity.  This establishes the identifying equalities with the independently defined causal fibers, rather than defining those fibers by the observed-law functional.

It remains to prove the qualified comparison in the final sentences.  Positivity of the eight cells with a fixed first coordinate gives
\[
 q_x=\sum_{y,z,w\in B}P(x,y,z,w)>0
 \qquad(x\in B). \tag{1}
\]
Therefore \(\mathrm{lem{:}bdg\text{-}weak\text{-}fiber\text{-}translation}\) applies.  Explicitly, from a weak legal model it forms
\[
 \pi_x(E)=q_x^{-1}\int_Eh_x(u)\,d\mu(u), \tag{2}
\]
and in the reverse direction it sets
\[
 \mu=\sum_{x\in B}q_x\pi_x,
 \qquad
 h_x=\frac{d(q_x\pi_x)}{d\mu}. \tag{3}
\]
The identities \(h_xd\mu=q_xd\pi_x\) prove equality of every path probability and of the unconditional APE, while leaving the feedback kernel unrestricted.  Combined with the comparator scope recorded in \(\mathrm{lem{:}bdg\text{-}continuous\text{-}feedback\text{-}program}\), this is precisely the claimed weak \(T=2\) measure-valued correspondence.

By the two legal-class definitions, every strict model satisfies all weak conditions and additionally satisfies strict initial and feedback positivity.  Hence the strict fiber is an additional subclass and is not attributed to the published weak fiber.  The reverse Stieltjes construction in the all-laws theorem is finite atomic in general.  Equations (2)--(3) preserve, rather than remove, atomic and singular components.  Since no declared result replaces every such representation by a Lebesgue-absolutely-continuous one while preserving the cells, APE, and feedback restrictions, no density-specialization equivalence follows.  This proves the corrected comparator and heterogeneity-law scope as well as the exact finite certificates.
